Turn row values into column names

Source: R/row-to-colnames.R
row_to_colnames.Rd

Tables extracted from PDFs, e.g. with tabulapdf, sometimes have their column names in the first row (or rows) and nondescript names above. row_to_colnames() replaces the column names by the values of those rows and drops the rows.

Usage

row_to_colnames(data, row = 1L, collapse = " ", drop = TRUE)

Arguments

data

Data frame or matrix.

row

Integer. Position of the row or rows that contain the column names. Default is 1.

collapse

String. Separator between the values of several rows. Default is " ".

drop

Logical. Should the rows be removed? Default is TRUE.

Value

data with new column names, as a data frame of the same class, or a tibble if data was a matrix.

Details

With several rows, their values are pasted together per column. Missing values, blank strings, "NA", and "NaN" are skipped, and whitespace around a value is trimmed; if all of a column's values in these rows are missing or blank, it keeps its name. The new names must be unique: a header that repeats, as in "M, SD, M, SD", is an error unless a second row tells the columns apart. A label that spans several columns, such as a group name above "M, SD", is often only in the first of them; repeat it in each one first.

See also

unheadr::mash_colnames(), a more general solution to the same problem.
